A1.justification: Both PDFs describe REST and contain readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting comparison. V1 ends after its references; v2 additionally contains appendices A-G, which were included in the comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original HDTF and MEAD experiments, component ablations and generated examples in Tables 1-3 and Figures 3-4.

after.justification: V2 retains the original quantitative experiments and adds qualitative ASD ablation and cross-actor generalization results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The architecture and caching/distillation framework remain. However, Eq. 21 now includes the positive pair in the contrastive denominator; Eq. 23 replaces a signed difference sum with mean squared teacher-student second-difference matching; and Eq. 24 introduces weights, specified as 0.2 each. Algorithm 1 also corrects chunk, timestep and cache indexing. These revise the documented procedure without establishing that the implementation or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: HDTF and MEAD remain the training and quantitative evaluation datasets. Appendix D adds limited qualitative coverage of stylized portraits and cross-actor driving, including cinematic speech with background noise and speech with natural reverberation.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains FantasyTalking, Hallo, EchoMimic, Sonic, AniPortrait, Ditto and AniTalker. Figure 4 retains its existing comparator subset. Appendix D introduces no new competing method; Full ASD and w/o ASD were already evaluated in Table 3.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported student training length from 121 to 97 frames. Sections 4.3-4.4 change ablation and case-study length descriptions from 120 to 121 frames. Appendix D adds qualitative comparisons with fixed portrait/audio inputs and matched training settings. The main benchmark metrics, 121-frame evaluation and eight-step sampling remain; rerunning is not established.

E4.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a qualitative Full ASD versus w/o ASD comparison examining degradation on a stylized portrait. Appendix D.2 adds visual generalization checks across portrait styles and acoustic conditions. These supplement the retained caching and distillation ablations with a limited set of qualitative analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix C.6.3 newly discloses sharing a random seed between teacher and student to generate matched Gaussian noise. This adds seed-handling information only: neither version reports independent-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: REST's reported runtime changes from 4.421 to 4.416 seconds in Table 1 and Figure 4. Table 3 changes w/o Contrastive FVD from 211.881 to 219.881, reversing its ordering against Full ASD at 219.870. Figures 8-10 add qualitative outputs. Other benchmark scores remain unchanged; the revisions do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Appendices C.1-C.3 introduce substantial formal analysis absent from v1: mutual-information invariance, an InfoNCE lower-bound derivation, velocity/content smoothness equivalence, the spectral penalty 16 sin^4(omega/2), and loss-complementarity arguments. These add assumptions, theorems and proofs beyond the revised main-text loss equations.

C1.justification: The introduction qualifies the novelty claim as, to the authors' knowledge, the first end-to-end real-time streaming talking-head diffusion method on a single GPU. Contributions and conclusion now foreground information-theoretic alignment and kinematic constraints for ASD. The central streaming, speed and quality claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands the mechanism explanation through mutual-information alignment and frequency-sensitive smoothness regularization. Appendix D interprets the new examples as evidence of stylistic and acoustic generalization. Appendix E adds previously absent concrete limitations: motion blur during rapid head movements and unclear dental details, attributed to training data and aggressive VAE compression.

D1.justification: Appendices A-C disclose extensive preprocessing, architecture, initialization and training details, including hierarchical Whisper features, cache dimensions, noise scheduling, dropout rates, loss temperature and weights, gradient accumulation, memory usage and approximately 400 GPU hours. Identity-disjoint splitting is newly specified, and Appendix F describes research-only access. These substantially expand reproducibility information without establishing that every disclosed component is newly introduced.

R1.justification: The principal THG positioning remains, with MultiTalk added to Section 2.2. New references connect ASD to contrastive predictive coding and mutual-information bounds, while others document preprocessing and architectural components. The novelty positioning is also qualified by the single-GPU condition.

P1.justification: V2 revises the abstract, contribution list and portions of the methods and conclusion, consistently introducing semi-autoregressive terminology. Extensive explanations of existing components are organized into cross-referenced appendices covering datasets, architecture, training, qualitative analysis, limitations and ethics. This substantially expands the document's explanatory structure.

P2.justification: Figures 5-7 add attention-pattern, SpeechAE and A2V-DiT diagrams. Figures 8-10 add an ASD ablation display and cross-actor generated-frame grids. These substantially expand the visual explanation and evidence; the original benchmark tables and Figures 1-4 largely retain their layouts.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially reduces v1's implementation ambiguity through detailed preprocessing, architecture and training disclosures, and repairs loss equations that did not match their stated teacher-student purpose. Additional qualitative checks and specific limitations improve assessability. The new theory is less conclusive than its wording suggests: Theorem C.2 assumes independent marginal negatives, whereas implementation uses same-sequence frames. Despite this qualification, the gains in methodological specification and transparency are substantial.
